fix(ios): message-delivery correctness + relay/limbo queue caps

Audit batch 1 (verified, build green):
- Group messages on the single receive path (ConversationStore.handleIncomingMessage) now decrypt via GroupKeyService instead of rendering raw base64 ciphertext (mirrors the batch handler).
- MeshACKHandler.isDuplicate is now read-only; the mesh receive path marks an ID seen only AFTER a successful DB insert, so a failed insert no longer burns the ID for 7 days and permanently drops re-sprayed copies. upsert/applyMessage failures now log in release.

fix(ios): gate cleartext fallbacks behind default-OFF flags (#97, #95)

Audit CRITICAL/HIGH (verified, build green):
- #97 (H8.F5): GroupService.broadcastKey's legacy plaintext group-key fallback (raw AES key in MeshEnvelope.text over BLE) now gated behind FeatureFlag.legacyPlaintextGroupKey (default OFF). Unrooted members get the key via the targeted ATSAM path after pairing instead of cleartext.
- #95 (H8.F1): mesh-receive 'render unknown wire as plaintext' fallback now gated behind FeatureFlag.legacyPlaintextRender (default OFF) AND no longer auto-promotes the sender to .suspectedLegacy — removing the durable confidentiality-downgrade lock-in. Default is the secure placeholder.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(ios): authenticate MPC peers via signed challenge (C2)

MPCTransportService accepted any peer whose displayName/fingerprint prefix matched (spoofable) and never called MPCAuthChallenge.verify() — so any nearby device could authenticate and inject bulk frames. Now gates authentication on await challenge.verify() (resolves the signer key from BLE-trusted devices, rejects unknown peers) plus a 5-minute replay window. Behavior change: MPC peers must be BLE-trusted first (the documented intent).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(ios): bind Club mesh-frame verification to pinned identity (C3)

ClubService handlePing/handleJoin/handleLeave verified the Ed25519 signature against the key supplied IN the frame, then trusted payload.userId — so any device could forge a signed frame claiming an arbitrary userId (member-location and membership spoofing). Each handler now additionally requires the frame's signer key to equal PeerKeyDirectory.identityKey(for: payload.userId) whenever that user's identity is pinned; mismatches are rejected. Echo/Vault use a different (anonymous/location-gated) model and are deferred for separate review.

fix(bridge): bind bridge sender identity + flag the recipient-PeerID gap

Two issues surfaced by the post-embed audit of the now-primary serverless
bridge path:

- LIBP2P-2 (security): MeshBridgeReceiver.decryptAndPublish verified only that
  the signature was internally valid against the self-supplied signerPublicKey —
  it never bound that key to the claimed senderId, so any peer reachable over the
  libp2p bridge could self-sign an envelope impersonating a contact. Add the same
  identity binding the BLE path uses (MeshCryptoService.verifySignature Step 2):
  reject when the sender already has known trusted devices and the signer isn't
  one of them; allow unknown senders (first-contact/TOFU), matching BLE posture.

- LIBP2P-1 (doc): document that uploadEnvelope's recipientHint is a user-ID hash,
  not yet a libp2p PeerID, so node.send's peer.Decode fails — the outbound bridge
  is a no-op until a recipientHint→PeerID resolver lands. BLE mesh + inbound
  bridge are unaffected. Marked as the key remaining bridge work.

Verified: app + tests build; full unit suite re-run (core crypto + mesh interop
all green; only unsigned-test-host keychain failures remain).

fix(atsam): persist the paired root so ATSAM actually protects messages

ATSAM-1 (audit): the hybrid X25519+ML-KEM pairing derived a root but never
stored it — ATSAMRootStorage.setRoot() had zero call sites — so
ATSAMMessageSealer.seal() always returned nil, every message silently fell back
to the legacy path, and NO live message was ever ATSAM-protected. Downstream,
GroupService.broadcastKey() shipped group keys in plaintext for every member
(its "sealed" path was dead).

Wire setRoot into both online pair-completion paths (the production transport;
ATSAMPairView is a dev scaffold and left alone):
- runOnlinePair (initiator): persist result.root keyed by the peer's userId.
- acceptPairInit (responder): persist keyed by init_.fromUser.
Keying matches the sealer contract — seal looks up root(for: recipientUserId),
unseal looks up root(for: senderUserId), both = the peer.

Also pass selfUserId/peerUserId into pairAsInitiator/pairAsResponder (ATSAM-4)
so the round-26 transcript userId bindings are populated on the live path
(defends confused-deputy / cross-pair replay). Both roles derive the same
transcript, so roots still agree.

Safe to activate: the receive path (MessageContentSealer) is magic-byte gated
and already wired to ATSAMMessageSealer.unseal — legacy messages are never
misrouted, and an ATSAM body with a missing root yields decryptFailed (not a
crash). No existing ATSAM roots exist to break (it was fully orphaned).

Verified: build SUCCEEDED; unit suite unchanged (core crypto + mesh interop
green). End-to-end pair→seal→unseal round-trip needs a code-signed run
(ATSAMRootStorage is Keychain-backed; the unsigned sim test host returns
errSecMissingEntitlement).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat(bridge): resolve recipient PeerID for libp2p outbound (LIBP2P-1)

The outbound bridge was a no-op: uploadEnvelope passed recipientHint straight to
node.send, which peer.Decode-rejects anything that isn't a libp2p PeerID.

Add a pure-Swift `Libp2pPeerID.fromEd25519` that reproduces go-libp2p's
`peer.IDFromPublicKey` (PublicKey protobuf → identity multihash → base58btc),
and resolve recipientHint in uploadEnvelope: pass a PeerID through untouched, or
treat it as a RAVEN userId and derive the contact's PeerID from their pinned
Ed25519 identity key (PeerKeyDirectory) — the same key their libp2p host boots
from, so it matches with no directory. Unroutable hints fail closed.

Verified: new unit test asserts the Swift derivation equals an authoritative
go-libp2p vector (Ed25519 seed 01..20 → 12D3KooWJ1Tsij…), generated by the added
Libp2pBridge/cmd/peeridvec helper. MeshInteropVectors 9/9 pass.

Remaining: the gateway-relay caller (MeshGatewayService) still forwards an opaque
neighbor-supplied hint; any caller that passes a userId or PeerID now works, so

fix(windows): port mediaSealed/gkv/pk into C# signingData (mesh interop)

The Windows C# SecureMeshEnvelope.SigningData() was missing three fields the iOS
canonical form emits, so iOS↔Windows Ed25519 mesh signatures failed to verify
(audit ATSAM-WIRE-1/2/3). Bring C# in line with iOS (the ground truth — iOS is
not changed):

- Add properties MediaSealed (JSON "msl"), GroupKeyVersion ("gkv"),
  PayloadKind ("pk").
- SigningData(): append MediaSealed unconditionally (empty when null) between
  audioDuration and replyToMessageId (round 26); after the GeoFence block append
  "gkv:<n>" then "pk:<s>" only when set (round 46) — exact iOS order.
- Update the C# interop vector to the iOS ground truth (10 trailing empty pipes
  after `text`, was 9). The GeoFence EndsWith test is unaffected.

NOT built locally (no .NET toolchain on this machine) — mechanical mirror of
iOS MeshCryptoService.swift:757,798-805. The updated C# test will confirm it on
the next Windows build. ACK + Stop envelopes were already consistent.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

harden(groups): release-visible audit log when plaintext group-key fires

feat(e2ee): serverless 1-RTT Noise IK seal so QR-only peers get readable E2E

LIVE-VERIFIED end-to-end (2 iOS sims + local relay): a message sealed by A now
DECRYPTS and renders as plaintext on B — two peers who only exchanged static keys
via QR, no server, no pairing handshake, delivered over the libp2p bridge.

Root cause: MessageContentSealer only had a transport-mode Noise path
(NoiseSessionStore.encrypt), which needs an ESTABLISHED session. QR-only peers
have none, so seal fell through to RVNP1 plaintext (actually: the chat skipped
wrapping entirely, shipping raw bytes), and the receiver's unseal saw no magic →
"[Encrypted message — could not decrypt]". The existing Noise IK handshake is
wired only over the BLE RUM-v2 binary path (noiseHandshake1/2 frames), which the
EncryptedMeshPayload bridge/legacy path never carries.

Fix — ride the body inside a self-contained Noise IK message-1 (1-RTT, fresh
ephemeral ⇒ forward secrecy), in the same MessageContentSealer wire the bridge
already carries:
- NoiseSessionStore.writeHandshake1Stateless / openHandshake1Stateless: write/read
  an IK M1 carrying the payload WITHOUT caching a session. Stateless keeps the
  scheme symmetric (each direction seals its own M1; never half-opens a session
  the peer can't complete with an M2 we don't round-trip).
- MessageContentSealer: new RVNH1 magic. seal() emits RVNH1+M1 when there's no
  transport session but we hold the recipient's static key (from the QR pin via
  PeerKeyDirectory). unseal() opens RVNH1 statelessly, enforces the recovered
  sender static == expected (anti-impersonation) and the same SealedReplayWindow
  (peerPID+msgId) guard as RVNS1.
- DeliveryJobRunner: treat RVNH1 as already-sealed so the bridge/mesh retry paths
  don't double-wrap.

Fixes serverless E2E for BOTH the libp2p bridge AND BLE mesh (same sealer). Once
a real Noise session exists (BLE pairing / ATSAM), seal() still prefers the
transport (RVNS1) path — RVNH1 is purely the first-contact fallback.

feat(mesh): sealed-sender v2 wire foundation + cross-platform parity (task_a1157777)

everything else builds on. This is the "read-before-write" stage the design
mandates ships FIRST — it is purely additive and emits NOTHING new (no broadcast
is sealed yet), so it cannot break any peer. sealFormat==nil reproduces today's
exact bytes.

the wire — never the raw ids that need local resolution.

  the hashes survive the broadcast wire (closes the "hashes lost" data-loss bug
  the design flagged as load-bearing).

  at position 4 (senderName dropped — receivers re-derive the display name from
  local contacts, never the wire), recipientIdHash at position 5, then a trailing

feat(media): serverless E2E attachments + voice over mesh/bridge (no server)

serverless, E2E-encrypted, over BLE mesh + the libp2p bridge.

  KEY (AES-GCM); the ciphertext rides in a new envelope field `mediaCipher`

  receive, the key opens the cipher, the bytes are written to a local cache file,

  Capped at 10 MB raw.
- `mediaCipher` added to MeshEnvelope + SecureMeshEnvelope (CodingKey "mc"),
  threaded through toSecure/toMesh, deliberately NOT in signingData (its own AEAD
  tag covers integrity; signing multi-MB would bloat every verify).
- toMeshEnvelope now carries the LOCAL file path as mediaUrl when there's no
  server URL, so the sealer can read + embed the bytes.
- DeliveryJobRunner: allow .image/.voice/.file on the mesh AND bridge channels

- bridge.go: maxEnvelopeBytes 64 KiB → 24 MiB so an embedded-media envelope fits

up to its physical chunk ceiling (~50 KB ⇒ voice notes / small images); larger
